segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: One of the things I really wanted to draw you on, on Haynesville, that 1966 case: in May 2025 you write in Forbidden Science 7 that whatever this phenomenon is, this isn't just about propulsion, it's not about materials either, or relativity, or quanta. You talk about how the phenomenon operates from higher reality levels and how it can reprocess human consciousness. And then, five months after that diary entry, at a talk at the Sol Foundation, a premier event discussing UAP science, I thought it was incredibly significant that the event you chose wasn't the Tic Tac, it was an event that had happened 60 years ago, the Haynesville case, at Christmas 1966. And I'm just wondering whether it's because you've got an object that's potentially emitting 1.4 gigawatts of luminous energy: by rights that forest should have been irradiated, completely destroyed by that kind of energy. But whatever the phenomenon was in that forest that night, it seemed to be able to control its physical effects, not just on human consciousness but also on the physical environment. And that, to me, Jacques, is what I find fascinating about what you drill in on, because there are those weird unexplained inconsistencies in the Haynesville case even 60 years on.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Well, we have a witness who was alive at the time, within feet of that source of energy: it's a tree. The witnesses went back, once they discovered the clearing, and the trees had been irradiated around the object, and they took bark from one of the trees. And then, being good scientists, they also went around the tree and took bark from the other side, and I have both samples — a fairly large amount — and one is completely black and the other one is a normal bark from the tree.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: For a long time I couldn't have it, because they sent it to an atomic research organization, which returned it. So I asked: did they send it back, what was it? And the witness told me: yeah, they sent it back with no comment, they had it for two years and they may have done something, but they didn't want to be involved, so they returned it. So I said: can I have it? He said sure. So he sent it to me and I've had it, but I didn't want it to be probed until there was a method that did not cut into the bark. It's a little bit like the Shroud of Turin: you can't cut a corner, the Pope says no, no, no, you do what you want with your physics, but the shroud is intact. Now those techniques exist, so that's why I've reopened that case, because without the testimony from the tree we don't have a good measure of the energy. The tree measured the energy, absorbed it, it was feet from the radiating object.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: By the way, the witnesses also canvassed the area. They found four other witnesses of similar observations in the sky. The Air Force said: well, this was on the ground, so give it to the Army, because it's not flying. Well, the others were flying. But of course, people don't report that kind of thing. Who is going to go to some university to report something? If you're the pharmacist in the village or in the town, or if you sell gasoline to truckers and so on, why would you expose your family and your business to saying that you were a witness of something like that? So I think the semi-disclosure that's coming is going to open that up: it's going to be respectable now to have seen a UFO. Of course there will be a flood of false cases, and we're back to the noise question that we discussed before.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Well, Dr. Jacques Vallée, I guess what you've just told me about Haynesville, a case that happened 60 years ago, underlines the absolute essence of Dr. Jacques Vallée: that you're not some guy who's just working through dusty archives that other people have acquired, you were intellectually engaged with this subject in the field from the very beginning of your life. And I can only say, from all of us, thank you so much for the great work that you've done and continue to do. Thank you for Forbidden Science 7. And may Dr. Jacques Vallée continue to intrigue and bemuse us with his cryptic comments in his diaries for many, many years to come.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I'll do my best, I promise.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Jacques, thank you so much, sir, much appreciated.
